clue.text: Tame budgie, preferable to wild ones?

definitions.text: Tame budgie, preferable to wild ones?

parts.words: Tame budgie, preferable to wild ones?
parts.note: a pet bird held is the proverb's sure thing, worth two in the bush, so it beats wild birds

explanation.surface: A bird-lover argues that a tame pet budgie is better than wild birds.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb runs 'a bird in the hand is worth two in the bush': the bird you hold beats the wild ones you might catch.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverbial phrase names something secure that you already possess, valued above uncertain prospects.

clue.text: See flow chart is repositioned straight

indicators.note: letters that are repositioned are moved into new places, so the four words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Instructions on reading a flow chart that has been rearranged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is repositioned' reads as the verb phrase; 'is' belongs to the fodder and 'repositioned' alone signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes the direct route between two points, so it means in a straight line.

clue.text: One translating Latin, a Roman, perhaps

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: translating turns words into another form, so the letters of Latin and a are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone translating Latin might be a Roman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translating' is the anagram signal for the second and third pieces. A Roman is only one example of the definition, which is why 'perhaps' is there.
explanation.definitionFit: Rome is in Italy, so a Roman is one example of a person from that country.

clue.text: Over the moon here to have secret room

parts.note: deep can mean hidden or mysterious, as in a deep secret
room means space, as in room to move

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled to have a secret room in their house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over the moon' looks like delighted; read literally, it means beyond the moon, the region the definition describes.
explanation.definitionFit: The far reaches of the universe lie beyond the moon, so this is where 'over the moon' places you.

clue.text: Joint titleholder

parts.note: a person holding a title, here a name, jointly with someone else

explanation.surface: Someone who shares a championship or a property deed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Titleholder' suggests a sports champion; the title shared here is simply a name.
explanation.definitionFit: A person called after another shares that person's name, so both hold it together.

clue.text: A flying shed?

parts.note: not a shed that flies but a large shed for flying machines

explanation.surface: A shed that has taken off into the air.
explanation.definitionFit: Aircraft are stored in this large shed-like building, so it is a shed for flying.

clue.text: Instructive sort of book couple picked up in house

indicators.note: in places the turned word within the house abbreviation
picked up means lifted, so in a down clue the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a couple is two

explanation.surface: A self-help book about two people setting up home together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' can suggest a sound-alike clue; in a down entry it means lifted upwards, a turnaround, and 'in' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A guide giving practical step-by-step instructions is a manual of this kind.

clue.text: Book every anaesthetist will have?

definitions.meaning: the fourth book of the Old Testament
an anaesthetist numbs patients, so the clue jokes that they have things that numb

explanation.surface: A book that every anaesthetist is meant to own.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the word as one who numbs, pronounced without the B sound changing.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bible's fourth book has this title, and anaesthetists deal in agents that make patients numb.

clue.text: With this you can get a handle on your gambling

definitions.text: With this you can get a handle on your gambling

parts.words: With this you can get a handle on your gambling
parts.note: the idiom 'get a handle on' means control, but literally this machine has a handle you pull to gamble

explanation.surface: Advice on getting your gambling habit under control.
explanation.definitionFit: A slot machine is worked by pulling a lever on its side, giving the gambler a literal handle.

clue.text: Shopkeeper, for example, exchanges staff

parts.note: to exchange goods is to trade them
to staff a post is to man it

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper swapping employees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' looks like a noun, but here it is the verb meaning to provide workers.
explanation.definitionFit: A shopkeeper is one example of a person who buys and sells goods for a living.

clue.text: Half of us succeeded, including me

indicators.note: including means holding within, so the word me goes inside

parts.note: to have won is to have succeeded

explanation.surface: A woman boasts that half the group, herself among them, succeeded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'including' signals the container. 'Half of us' is fair because roughly half of all people are female.
explanation.definitionFit: Roughly half of humanity is female, so the female sex is half of us.

clue.text: Initially short period going over issues

indicators.note: going over suggests turning round, so the word for period is read backwards

parts.note: a period is a length of time

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter of short is used

explanation.surface: A short period of reviewing problems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going over' turns TIME into EMIT; 'Initially' takes S from short. 'issues' looks like a noun but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue something is to send it out or give it off, the same as discharging it.

clue.text: Good clean entertainment? Not musical, though

definitions.text: Good clean entertainment? Not musical, though

parts.words: Good clean entertainment? Not musical, though
parts.note: good clean suggests cleaning and so soap, entertainment suggests a show set to music, but this serial drama has no singing

explanation.surface: Praise for wholesome entertainment that is not a musical.
explanation.walkthrough: Such serials were sponsored by detergent makers, hence 'clean'; the second half of the name means a sung drama, which this is not.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-running TV or radio drama serial was named after its soap-manufacturer sponsors, though it has no music.

clue.text: As directed, fires rifles

parts.note: to run a company is to direct it
to fire someone is to sack them

explanation.surface: Someone fires rifles as instructed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rifles' and 'fires' both look like gunfire; 'rifles' is the verb meaning searches through, and 'fires' means dismisses.
explanation.definitionFit: To rifle a place is to search it thoroughly to steal, the same as plundering it.

clue.text: Takes plane (American), which lands in the sea

parts.note: to jet somewhere is to travel by plane

explanation.surface: An American catches a flight that ends in a sea landing.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the material thrown overboard from a ship, which ends up in the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods discarded overboard from a ship to lighten it end up floating in or sinking into the sea.

clue.text: Watch next to key, a surprising sight

parts.note: to eye something is to watch it
a key is something that opens a lock

explanation.surface: A watch next to a key makes an unexpected sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Watch' looks like a timepiece but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Something revealing and astonishing is an experience that widens your gaze in shock.

clue.text: Di abandons hazy intuition

indicators.note: abandons means leaves behind, so these two letters drop out of the longer word

parts.note: hazy means unclear or blurred
taken as written

explanation.surface: Princess Di gives up on a vague hunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandons' takes DI out of INDISTINCT.
explanation.definitionFit: A gut feeling that comes without reasoning is an inborn sense of what is true.

clue.text: One may be caught out, losing this

definitions.text: One may be caught out, losing this

parts.words: One may be caught out, losing this
parts.note: in cricket a batsman caught by a fielder is out and so loses this

explanation.surface: A warning that someone caught out may lose something.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, when a batsman is caught out the fielding side takes one of these, and the batting side loses it.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a dismissal is counted as one of these taken, so a batsman caught out loses it.

clue.text: Small country's boast whole continent listened to

indicators.note: listened to means heard rather than read, so the words are what they sound like

parts.note: to crow is to boast, and Asia is a whole continent

explanation.surface: A small nation's boasting was heard across a whole continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'listened to' says that CROW plus ASIA, spoken, give the name.
explanation.definitionFit: This Balkan nation on the Adriatic has only a few million people.

clue.text: Like an open field, not sold illegally?

definitions.meaning: a fence is a dealer in stolen goods, so goods never passed to one were not fenced

explanation.surface: An open field described as never having been sold illegally.
explanation.walkthrough: A fence is slang for someone who sells stolen goods; to fence goods is to sell them on.
explanation.definitionFit: An open field has no boundary barrier, and loot never sold through a dealer was never handled that way.

clue.text: Monsters with poisonous gas defeat one

parts.note: CO is the chemical formula for carbon monoxide, a poisonous gas
a defeat is a loss
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Monsters armed with poison gas defeat someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Enormous statues or giants of any kind are huge things, akin to monstrous creatures.

clue.text: Clumsy French drive on it over here

definitions.text: French drive on it over here
definitions.meaning: the French word for left, and in Britain cars drive on the left

explanation.surface: A clumsy complaint about the French driving on our side here.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is the French word for left, the side on which traffic drives in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means socially awkward in English and is the French adjective for left-hand.

clue.text: Marks tool badly in hurry

indicators.note: badly means in a poor or wrong way, so the letters of marks and tool are disarranged

explanation.surface: A sloppy tool leaves marks when you rush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges MARKS TOOL.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an informal British command meaning be quick about it.

clue.text: In Scottish island, install parking app

indicators.note: to install is to fit something in, so the parking letter goes inside the island

parts.note: Skye is an island of the Scottish Inner Hebrides
P is the abbreviation for parking, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Someone on a Scottish island wants to install a parking app.
explanation.walkthrough: 'install' puts P inside SKYE.
explanation.definitionFit: This video-calling program is a piece of software for phones and computers.

clue.text: Top honours cut back in a series of steps

indicators.note: back means returning, so the combined letters are read in reverse

parts.note: in card games the ace and king are the top honour cards, A and K
to lop is to cut

explanation.surface: The highest awards are cut back in a sequence of stages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns AKLOP round. 'Top honours' looks like awards; in bridge the honours are the high cards, of which ace and king are top.
explanation.definitionFit: This lively Bohemian dance is a set pattern of footwork, a sequence of steps.

clue.text: List of competitors is in lobby

definitions.meaning: the full set of contestants in a race or competition

explanation.surface: A list of competitors is posted in the lobby.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means the field of contestants entered in an event and also a hall by a front door.

clue.text: Charlie soon with new side: made one of the Saints

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
anon is an old word for soon

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh version, so the letters of side are rearranged

explanation.surface: A player called Charlie soon joins a new team and becomes a Saint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns SIDE into ISED. 'Saints' suggests a football club (Southampton are the Saints), but the definition is about sainthood.
explanation.definitionFit: A person declared a saint by the Church has been formally raised to sainthood.

clue.text: One's designs appear on flags

parts.note: flags here are flagstones, the paving slabs where a street chalk artist draws

explanation.surface: A designer whose patterns appear on national flags.
explanation.walkthrough: Flags is short for flagstones, the slabs of a footpath.
explanation.definitionFit: A street artist draws chalk pictures on the paving slabs of the footway for passers-by.
